<section class="story-box" aria-labelledby="planning-heading">
## How to use Exploration {#planning-heading}

Exploration is a **what-if sketchpad**, not a flight forecast. Try changing a seasonal cell, route distance or flight count, or delay and cancellation values to see how a scenario appears. Aviators can use it to frame questions about seasonal patterns and disruptions; travelers can use it to think about timing and possible delays. For real decisions, check current airline information and official aviation and weather guidance.

<section class="story-box" aria-labelledby="cells-heading">
## What the cells show {#cells-heading}

Each seasonal cell is a **hypothetical index from 0 to 100**, not a count of flights or minutes of delay. Select a month and measure, then enter an index: the selected cell updates, and its color becomes more opaque as the value rises. The row’s color identifies the measure; the shade makes the entered value easier to compare visually. Other cells stay unchanged. These illustrative starting values help demonstrate the interaction—they are not calculated from flight records.

<svg class="story-visual" viewBox="0 0 760 185" role="img" aria-label="A hypothetical index value controls the opacity of a seasonal heatmap cell">
